nodes.label: column_definition catch-all arm
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same claim, counted independently in this session. The listed arms of column_definition in crates/snipset-cli/src/db/init.rs cover only some names; everything else falls to `_ => format!("{column} TEXT")` and is emitted as a bare nullable TEXT. That is how twelve columns come out with the wrong declared type, NOT NULL flag, or DEFAULT compared with what the desktop app declares, including research_tag which the app declares INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L28] `snipset init` builds its `CREATE TABLE` from the same constants that form the CLI's schema fingerprint (`crates/snipset-cli/src/db/fingerprint.rs`, consumed by `create_table` in `crates/snipset-cli/src/db/init.rs`). Those constants are only column NAMES. The type of each emitted column comes from `column_definition` in `init.rs`, which has a catch-all `_ => format!("{column} TEXT")`. Several columns therefore come out with the wrong declared type or the wrong DEFAULT compared to what the desktop app declares, and because the fingerprint only compares names, every existing test still passes.

nodes.label: A schema parser that yields zero columns must fail the test loudly
nodes.norm_label: a schema parser that yields zero columns must fail the test loudly
nodes.summary: Vacuity guard on the narrow parsers. Both the CREATE TABLE block reader and the migration-array reader assert their anchor occurs exactly once and assert the extracted column list is non-empty, so a parser that silently stops matching (anchor renamed, indentation changed, array restructured) turns the test red instead of green. The task also required a column definition to fail to parse rather than be skipped, in the narrow-parser-fails-loudly style already used in fingerprint_test.rs.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L53] 8. Guard against a vacuous test. If the parser yields zero columns for a table, the test must fail loudly rather than pass. `fingerprint_test.rs` has an existing precedent for this; follow it.

nodes.label: NOT NULL is read from an explicit token pair, never inferred from PRIMARY KEY
nodes.norm_label: not null is read from an explicit token pair, never inferred from primary key
nodes.summary: Judgement call recorded in the final report. The notnull expectation is set only by an adjacent NOT NULL token pair in the app's declaration. It is deliberately not derived from a PRIMARY KEY clause, which is what a reader would otherwise assume.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L09145] SQLite's `pragma_table_info` reports `notnull=0` for a `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so inferring would have manufactured false failures on both `uuid` columns.

nodes.label: Default literals compared with one outer quote pair stripped from both sides, none kept distinct from empty
nodes.norm_label: default literals compared with one outer quote pair stripped from both sides, none kept distinct from empty
nodes.summary: Judgement call on dflt_value comparison. The app-side literal is kept verbatim including its quotes because pragma_table_info returns DEFAULT 'Text' as 'Text' with quotes. For the comparison itself one matching outer quote pair is stripped from both sides, so a pure quoting difference cannot fail the test, while the <none> sentinel stays distinct from the empty literal so DEFAULT '' and no default remain different facts. Raw literals are printed in the failure report.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9144] - **`DEFAULT 'Text'`**: kept verbatim including quotes on the app side, since `dflt_value` returns `'Text'` with quotes. For *comparison* I strip one matching outer quote pair from **both** sides so a quoting difference alone cannot fail the test, but `<none>` stays distinct from the empty literal, so `DEFAULT ''` and no default remain different facts. Raw literals are printed in the failure report.

nodes.label: schema.rs and the migration arrays currently agree, so the reconciliation disagreement branch never fires
nodes.norm_label: schema.rs and the migration arrays currently agree, so the reconciliation disagreement branch never fires
nodes.summary: The test reconciles two sources into one expectation per column: the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS groups/snippets blocks in schema.rs, which are authoritative for a fresh database, and the group_cols / snippet_cols migration arrays, which cover columns added after the table was created. Where a column appears in both, the two parsed shapes are compared and a disagreement is reported rather than one being silently preferred. Measured result for groups (12 columns) and snippets (26 columns): the two sources agree on every shared column, is_deleted being INTEGER DEFAULT 0 in both and image_data TEXT in both, so the disagreement branch is implemented but currently dead.

nodes.label: A hand-written simulation of the parser misled the fix: filter instead of take_while produced a false alarm
nodes.norm_label: a hand-written simulation of the parser misled the fix: filter instead of take_while produced a false alarm
nodes.summary: The declared-type parser was briefly changed to also stop at NULL and KEY, with a doc comment claiming this was needed to prevent false failures on TEXT NOT NULL and TEXT PRIMARY KEY. Re-running the simulation with the original keyword-only terminator set gave identical output on every sample, which falsified the premise. take_while stops at NOT and at PRIMARY and never reaches their operands, so the original code was already correct; the Python simulation had used a filter comprehension, which does keep scanning, and that was the actual defect. Both edits were reverted and the inaccurate comment removed.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9146] - **Declared type**: leading token run up to the first constraint keyword via `take_while`. I briefly "fixed" this to also stop at `NULL`/`KEY`, then reverted: `take_while` already stops at `NOT`/`PRIMARY` and never reaches their operands. My simulation had used a filter, which is what produced the false alarm.
